title: Cavity method for permutation models on Cayley trees
abstract: Motivated by permutation statistical models arising in random tensor networks, we study permutation models on a Cayley tree whose variables take values in the symmetric group $\Sn$. The pair interaction is assumed to depend only on the cycle type of the relative permutation. Then the Boltzmann weight is written as a class function on $\Sn$. This property diagonalizes the edge convolution operator in irreducible representation sectors. As a result, the linear stability of the uniform paramagnetic cavity solution is controlled by the character eigenvalue ratios. For cycle-factorized weights, these eigenvalues can be expressed as specializations of Schur functions. We derive the instability criteria and also verify their validity by comparison with direct numerical iterations of the cavity equation.
summary: This paper studies permutation spin models on Cayley trees by applying the cavity method. It uses representation theory to diagonalize the system's transfer operator, yielding analytic criteria for phase transitions based on character eigenvalue ratios. The results allow researchers to predict critical points in these complex statistical mechanical systems.
main_problem: The research analyzes permutation statistical models defined on a Cayley tree structure to determine their critical points and stability regimes.
main_result: The linear stability of the uniform paramagnetic solution is controlled by character eigenvalue ratios derived from diagonalizing the edge convolution operator. The method provides analytic criteria for phase transitions in these complex spin systems.
method: The cavity method, combined with non-commutative Fourier transforms using irreducible representations of the symmetric group $S_n$, is employed to linearize the homogeneous recursion equation around the paramagnetic state.
model_or_system: The model is a permutation spin system where variables take values in the symmetric group $S_n$. The interaction weights are assumed to be class functions on $S_n$, leading to an edge convolution operator that can be diagonalized in representation space.
key_observables: Local stability condition derived from character eigenvalue ratios ($\omega_\lambda / \omega_{[n]}$), and order parameters like Potts-like magnetization ($m_{id}(\eta)$) and standard-representation magnetization ($m_{	ext{std}}(\eta)$).
important_parameters: The coordination number $z$ of the Cayley tree, the size of the group $n$, and the coupling constants embedded in the weight function $W(g)$.
main_assumptions: The weights are assumed to be class functions on $S_n$. The analysis relies on approximating bulk critical behavior using the Bethe/Cayley-tree approximation, which may fail for entanglement transitions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates how the magnetization of the cavity fixed point evolves as a function of inverse temperature $ eta$ for various models, showing distinct flow regimes relative to the analytically derived instability points.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first setting up the model and applying the cavity method. It then uses representation theory to diagonalize the transfer operator, deriving stability criteria based on eigenvalue ratios. Finally, it verifies these analytic results through direct numerical iteration of the cavity equations for specific models.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, mathematically rigorous framework (using group representation theory) to analyze phase transitions in complex lattice/tree structures that are far beyond simple mean-field treatments, connecting statistical mechanics to advanced algebraic methods.
